key: e:test and evaluation master plan temp
synopsis: A Test and Evaluation Master Plan (TEMP) is an overarching document connecting planned virtual and physical tests to the decisions they inform, along with required data, resources, schedule and pass criteria [f16406]. It also links program decisions to test objectives, metrics, entrance and exit criteria, and reporting [f16408]. Its core device, the Integrated Decision Support Key, connects each decision to an evaluation question and the data needed to answer it, a method also described in Chapter 12 [f16409, f9813]. Chapter 12 classifies TEMP alongside NASA-STD-7009B, NATM and V&V planning as documented practice grounded in institutional standards and guidance, but the glossary reports that outcome studies comparing TEMP with alternatives were not found [f10136, f16411]. For the eleven-month collision-mitigation validation program, the glossary judges a literal defense TEMP excessive, distinguishing the useful planning logic from the suitability of its full implementation [f16412, f16409].

relations.note: Both describe the Integrated Decision Support Key linking decisions, evaluation questions and required data.
Adds objectives, metrics, entrance and exit criteria, and reporting to the overarching plan definition.
